validity.recommendation: Add 'Budince Pipeline' to OtherEnglishNames — this is the border-crossing name used in trade press (ICIS) and is even recorded as an alias on GEM's own wiki page ('also known as ... the Budince Pipeline'). Not a duplicate of any other roster row; it is the SAME physical asset under a second name, so no merge/split action needed, just an alias fill for future search-ability.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real and well-documented. Independently confirmed by (1) Kyiv Post/Interfax-Ukraine (28 Apr 2014), (2) Eustream's own inauguration press release (2 Sep 2014 ceremony at the Velke Kapusany compressor station, attended by EU rep Klaus-Dieter Borchardt, Slovak PM Robert Fico, Ukrainian PM Arseniy Yatsenyuk), (3) Eustream's own commercial-operation press release (2 Sep 2014), and (4) ICIS (30 Jun 2020), which describes it as 'the Budince interconnector, a single 700mm pipeline, which was quickly built by Eustream in 2013.' The ICIS piece cannot be cited (fails url_verifier — 200 but stub/paywalled body, ~210-850 chars depending on run) but was readable via a different fetch path for research purposes only, per standing rule 3. Confirmed via GEM's own wiki page text that 'Budince Pipeline' is the SAME asset as 'Vojany-Uzhgorod,' not a separate line — no duplicate risk. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission interconnector pipeline, Slovakia->Ukraine, built to enable reverse-flow gas imports (Eustream funded it entirely from its own resources, no EU/Slovak subsidy, per its own press release). DUPLICATE CHECK against the 39-row roster: not the same asset as P3063 (Uzhgorod-Velke Kapusany, a separate/larger 1400mm interconnection route at a different physical corridor, whose only shared feature is also touching the Uzhhorod area) or P0780 (Uzhhorod-Berehove, an internal Ukrainian branch line to a different destination). No merge or split recommended. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1='Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine' matches the TSO's own legal name (tsoua.com key-facts page, verified via Wayback capture: 'Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine, Limited Liability Company'). Owner2='eustream' matches the documented operator/funder of the Slovak-side leg. This split (Ukrainian-state TSO for the Ukrainian leg, national TSO of the other country for the foreign leg) is the correct pattern for a genuinely cross-border interconnector per the country's standing ownership rule -- no Gazprom attribution issue here since this crossing is Slovakia-Ukraine, not Russia-Ukraine. SPEC: Capacity (10.00 bcm/y) and StartYear1 (2014) both confirmed directly by Eustream's own commissioning statement; see separate spec note on the superseded preliminary capacity estimate. Diameter (700mm) is plausible and matches GEM's own wiki citation, but that citation (ICIS) fails independent verification here -- see the Diameter fill, staged UNRESOLVED rather than forcing an uncitable source. Length is blank in GEM and blank/unstated in every source checked -- correctly left blank rather than estimated.

validity.recommendation: No change to Capacity (keep 10.00 bcm/y). Do not treat the 8-9 bcm/y figure as a live conflict -- it is a superseded preliminary estimate from the same origin, not an independent competing claim.
validity.researcher_notes: Kyiv Post/Interfax-Ukraine (28 Apr 2014, five months BEFORE commissioning) quoted Eustream's own network chief giving a preliminary technical estimate: the pipeline would be used 'at a maximum capacity of 8-9 billion cubic meters of gas per year.' At the actual commercial launch (2 Sep 2014), Eustream's own press release gives the confirmed, more precise figure: 'Vojany-Uzhorod pipeline will transport to Ukraine 10 bcm of natural gas per year (27 mcm/day)... The full capacity of 10 bcm/year...', with a minimum guaranteed volume of 6.4 bcm/y (17.6 mcm/day) from 1 Oct 2014 and firm capacity from 1 Mar 2015. GEM's value (10.00 bcm/y) matches the final authoritative figure exactly. Both numbers trace to the same origin (Eustream), so per the corroboration rule this is NOT two independent sources agreeing on 10 -- it is one source (Eustream) whose own estimate evolved between April and September 2014. Flagged for transparency, not as an unresolved conflict.

validity.recommendation: Leave Diameter [ref] UNRESOLVED rather than cite a source that fails the verifier. If a future pass has ICIS access some other way, or finds an Eustream technical/network-map source with a diameter figure, add it then.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's own wiki page cites ICIS (the same 'Budince interconnector' article discussed above) as its sole source for Diameter=700mm ('single 700mm pipeline, which was quickly built by Eustream in 2013'). That source is real and was readable via an alternate fetch path for lead-following, but it fails scripts/url_verifier.py every time tried (200 status but a 210-850 byte stub body -- a bot-block/paywall, not a 404) and per the hard requirement 'every URL passes url_verifier.py before going in the xlsx,' it cannot be cited. No alternative source with an explicit diameter figure was found (Kyiv Post and both Eustream press releases give capacity but not diameter). Weak circumstantial corroboration only: ENTSOG/GIE System Capacity Map 2026 (sources/entsog/, already in this repo) classifies an operational pipeline strand in the Vojany/Uzhhorod border corridor (~22.22 E, 48.60 N) as its 'DN600-900 (24 to 36 in)' size class, which 700mm (~27.6 in) falls within -- consistent with, but not independent proof of, the exact 700mm figure. Net effect: the GEM value is plausible and not contradicted, but currently has NO independently verifiable public citation. Staged as UNRESOLVED, not as a value change.

fills.researcher_notes: Eustream's own press release documents commercial operation beginning 2 Sep 2014. No source found confirming continued operation past 2014-2020 specifically for this line (an ICIS piece from 30 Jun 2020 that does confirm active 2020 use of this exact crossing fails url_verifier as a stub/blocked page and cannot be cited). No evidence of closure or decommissioning was found anywhere, and per the country's standing rule, the 2025 end of Russian transit through Ukraine does not itself imply this reverse-flow import line (which never carried Russian transit gas -- it exists specifically to bring EU-sourced gas INTO Ukraine) went offline. Status=operating is retained on the strength of the commissioning source plus absence of any contrary reporting; flagged that a fresher confirmation would strengthen this.

Both Eustream (operator, 'transport to Ukraine 10 bcm of natural gas per year') and Kyiv Post/Interfax-Ukraine ('reverse supplies of natural gas from Slovakia to Ukraine') independently and explicitly describe this as a natural-gas pipeline. Two independent origins, both agreeing -- high tier.

Eustream's own press release is dated 02.09.2014 and states commercial operation began that day. Kyiv Post/Interfax-Ukraine (28 Apr 2014) independently forecasts launch in September 2014 reaching max capacity in October 2014 -- consistent with, and independently corroborating, StartYear1=2014. Two independent origins agreeing on the year -- high tier. (No month field forced; Eustream's release supports month=September if a StartMonth1 fill is later wanted.)

Eustream's own commercial-operation press release states the exact figure: '10 bcm of natural gas per year (27 mcm/day)' as full capacity, with 6.4 bcm/y (17.6 mcm/day) guaranteed minimum from Oct 2014 and firm service from Mar 2015. This is a single (though highly authoritative -- the pipeline's own operator) source; see the paired validity note on the superseded 8-9 bcm/y preliminary Eustream estimate reported by Kyiv Post, which traces to the same origin and so does not count as independent corroboration. Tier medium, not high.
